stem: Draw the straight line through $A({=x1}, {=y1})$ and $B({=x2}, {=y2})$.
solution: Find the gradient between A and B: m = (y2 − y1) / (x2 − x1).
Keep the sign of each difference exactly as it comes out — do not drop a sign when a coordinate is already negative.
Starting from A, step according to that gradient (rise over run) to fix the line's direction.
notes:
Tests the geometric core of LO1 (the unique line two points determine) rather than the symbolic y = mx + c form; graded on the property (any two collinear points are correct, FR-1205). Anchor ex8-6-10a's own points (A(-6,1)) fall outside the instrument's ±5 lattice limit, so instance parameters were rescaled to the same gradient family (1/3) while two further instances stress negative coordinates and a whole-number gradient. intercept-wrong and vertical-line are valid predicates for this kind but have no clean, non-strained match among this LO's own misconceptions, so they are left undiagnosed rather than forced.

PIPELINE NORMALISATION (not an author edit): drop-dead-predicate: dropped slope-inverted → mc:g10m8s3-2-1:gradient-formula-inversion, slope-sign-flipped → mc:g10m8s3-2-1:negative-coordinate-subtraction-slip — line_drawer with mode=points can never emit them (contract can_emit; consistency review W1); drop-opening-instance: instance 3 {"x1": -2, "y1": -3, "x2": 4, "y2": 3}: the point (-2, -3) swapped is (-3, -2), where a handle opens — an untouched handle would read as a swapped point (pipeline rule A10, stricter than the app).

PIPELINE NORMALISATION (not an author edit), data-engineer agent 2026-09-27, consistency review W1: removed solution step 4 ("Any two points lying on this same line are an acceptable construction — it is the line itself that is graded, not the two named points."). It is false for this widget: in "points" mode the line_drawer grades the two named points, not the line (widget-docs.ts: "there the two named points ARE the answer"), so a student who followed it would be marked wrong. The author was misled by the pipeline's old paraphrase of the instrument; the "graded on the property" remark above is wrong for the same reason. Removal only, so the blind verifier's verdicts carry (verified_as); the other steps are unchanged.
